edits.text: - When a finite verb or auxiliary is immediately followed (no intervening punctuation) by a short complement or direct object of ≤4 words that completes the predicate or fixes polarity, keep the verb/auxiliary joined to that following span.

Keep a numeral or measurement (digits or spelled-out number, including an immediately adjacent parenthetical equivalent) together with its immediately following unit or parenthetical equivalent; treat the number and its unit as one segmentation unit.

- Prefer a cut after a clear clause boundary or punctuation (for example sentence-final punctuation, a clause-ending comma, or the position immediately before a coordinating conjunction that begins a new clause) over a cut immediately after a finite verb or auxiliary when that verb/auxiliary is followed with no intervening punctuation by a short complement or direct object (roughly ≤4 words).

- Fallback ordering: when a numeral or measurement (digits or spelled-out number) is immediately adjacent to its unit or an immediately adjacent parenthetical equivalent (for example "55,000 barrels (2.3 million gallons)" or "1.5 hour"), prefer a cut after the unit or after the closing parenthesis over any cut located between the numeral and its unit.
